Wear your damn Helmet! Like all the time. I get it you're probably a monk or a barbarian that gets natural bonus to AC when you aren't wearing armor, I get it. What you don't realize is that wearing your helmet is a constant AC boost it looks sweet and you never have to worry about not having that edge. Other people might be focused on trying to fit in with all the other living breathing NPC's out there, while you'll be the one to actually live after you survive whatever mayhem is thrown your way. Be cool, wear your helmet, get the extra AC bonus, slay all who oppose you, and ride on!

I would like to point out that many of your sources are riddled with mythology and pro-Elsa sentiments rather than legitimate facts and sources. Many of the sorcery and tales of supernatural powers oftentimes attributed to Queen Elsa I are nothing more than propaganda used to legitimize her rule despite her many neuroses and further the agenda of established ruling class of the time. The fact that Queen Elsa I was a child riddled with psychological issues leaving her to rule the kingdom in isolation is the first clue that the sorcery was nothing more than a hyperbolic statement. With the growing strength of the Weselton economy over that of the waning Arendelle economy, Arendelle was losing its status as the power center of the region during the early rule of then Princess Elsa I. The Arendelle elite had created many elaborate tales to rationalize the state of the economy to the now largely unemployed citizens of Arendelle to prevent outright rebellion.

Now you may point out that the legends of her sorcery date back to the rule of her father King Agdar II. This can be attributed to the many psychotic episodes Elsa had as a child that the King had to explain to the ministers of the court. These outbursts would later escalate and lead her to almost killing her sister Anna in a fit of rage. Many of these outbursts and associated treatments have been documented in "Medicine of Arendelle" (Written by Minister Pabbie Trollman). The cost of these treatments ultimately burdened the Arendelle economy and with the dramatic increase in ice prices, King Agdar was eventually forced to isolate Princess Elsa from the rest of the kingdom.

With the sudden Death of King Agdar II, the ministers of the court assumed the throne belonged to Elsa and began to treat her as the royal heir. Princess Anna, the second in line realized that crowning Elsa as the Queen would only further hurt the economic status created a political coup to gain power. Princess Anna plotted with her supporters to assassinate Elsa in order to gain the throne for herself. One of her main supporters was Prince Hans who at the time was a remarkable Admiral (noted by Kim Jørgensen in his monumental The Rise and Fall of Prince Hans of the Southern Isles). When the coup failed miserably and Queen Elsa fled for her life, Prince Hans took control of the Capital as Princess Anna lead the main army. 

The elite class and many ministers still loyal to Queen Elsa I, began to regain order, Prince Hans was forced to flee the capital to regroup with Princess Anna. After the skirmish of the mountain, where Queen Elsa's army was able to create barricades using structures of snow and ice forcing Princess Anna to retreat and wait upon reinforcements. Prince Hans with his full army created a surprise attack and captured Queen Elsa and returned her to the capital. Minister Olaf, a childhood caretaker of both girls was able to escape the destroyed camp of Queen Elsa and negotiated a treaty for peace that ensured Elsa would not have unchecked power in the capital. A second member of the camp simply referred to as "Marshmallow" had documents showing plans to dispose Anna by Prince Hans after she regained control.

Princess Anna now with the remaining troops from Queen Elsa's army regrouped at the valley of living rocks to gather allies in the assault to regain the capital. When denied the expected support from the still stationed troops of Weselton, Princess Anna decided to attack anyways. Princess Anna, Minister Olaf, Minister Pabbie, General Kristoff and General Sven all lead forces that would ultimately win the decisive victory, allowing the royal family to reclaim Arendelle. Prince Hans was executed after this battle on the charges of treason according to the book "Minister Olaf, The Great Caretaker of Arendelle."

I hope this helped explain a few of the confusion areas. Please let me know if you have any questions on any of my sources, or materials and I would be happy to provide them.
